Thanks for taking the call today, John — appreciated the context on the knowledge-base use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan going into the POC:

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Answer accuracy >= 85% on the 500-sample KB test set (as judged by your SME rubric)
- Latency p90 < 350ms for single-turn queries under our expected load profile
- Hallucination rate < 2% (critical questions flagged by Acme SMEs)
- Business metric: 20% reduction in average handle time on support KB lookups in pilot period

Proposed evaluation approach:
1) Offline eval (week 1) — run candidate models against labeled test set you provided; generate confusion points and grading spreadsheet.
2) Online shadow (week 2) — shadow traffic to compare live behavior vs baseline (no customer-facing changes).
3) Pilot (week 3) — small cohort ramp, measure business metrics and error modes; iterate on prompts and cache settings.

I've attached a draft eval plan and a mutual action plan that maps timeline and owners (acme-poc-eval-plan.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx). Key asks from your side:
- Confirm the 500-sample test set and owner for labeling (SME contact)
- Confirm target SLA for latency and any regional constraints
- Access details for a read-only test environment (or a sample of anonymized KB entries)

Can we lock in the week-of July 6 start? If that works I’ll coordinate the kickoff and loop in engineering resources.

> Thanks for taking the call today, John — appreciated the context on the knowledge-base use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan going into the POC:
>

> - Latency p90 < 350ms for single-turn queries under our expected load profile
> - Hallucination rate < 2% (critical questions flagged by Acme SMEs)
> - Business metric: 20% reduction in average handle time on support KB lookups in pilot period

Proposed detailed eval steps (high level)
1) Offline eval (Day 1–3)
   - Objective: quickly rule out models that fail basic QA criteria and produce a ranked spreadsheet for SME review.
   - Inputs: 500-sample labeled set (Acme), existing baseline logs (sample), model candidates (open variants we discussed).
   - Outputs: per-sample model outputs, automated scoring (exact match, F1 where applicable), and SME disagreement flags.

2) Shadow eval (Day 4–10)
   - Objective: measure live behavior against baseline without routing to end users. Compare latency, throughput, and divergence on edge cases.
   - Shadow config: 10% of traffic routed in parallel to Redwood endpoint; sampling at peak and off-peak.
   - Metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency, token cost, error/hallucination counts (SME tagging), and business metric proxy (time to first useful suggestion).

3) Pilot (Day 11–21)
   - Objective: small cohort pilot with direct user exposure, monitor business impact and refine prompts/cache/quantization as needed.
   - Rollout: 5% then 25% of selected workflow.

Grading rubric (proposed — please align with your SMEs):
- Accuracy (weighted 40%) — SME-graded correctness on canonical answers.
- Relevance/Utility (weighted 25%) — SME scores if response helps resolve the query.
- Latency (weighted 15%) — p90 target used to score penalty bands.
- Hallucination rate (weighted 10%) — fraction of responses with fabricated facts per SME flag.
- Cost/Token efficiency (weighted 10%) — token ratio vs baseline.

Ownership and immediate asks:
- Acme: deliver labeled 500-sample set (Samantha) and provide shadow API key (IT).
- Redwood: provide offline eval artifacts, run shadow harness, and deliver weekly dashboard with per-sample flags (Dylan).
- CS (Rachel): own pilot user cohort and business metric tracking.

Timeline (proposed)
- July 6: Kickoff and environment handoff
- July 7–9: Offline eval run and SME review
- July 10–16: Shadowing + weekly sync
- July 17–23: Pilot ramp and business metric measurement

Links: evaluation plan in Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ACME-POC-EVAL-PLAN) and mutual action plan in HubSpot (linked in the doc).

I'll attach a short template CSV for the SME grading to keep labels consistent. Let me know if you'd like different weightings on the rubric or additional business KPIs.

Thanks — I can run the offline eval on July 7 if we have the first labeled batch by Friday.
